facebook:
Monday started on paper: a long on 2 ES for +$500.

Tuesday was day 1 on a funded account. The Asian session gave me a 3.5 point loss and a 2 point win. London was where I tried out my strategy, and by the close the account sat $100 higher.

Wednesday went back to paper. I read the direction wrong on the first entry and took a 4 point stop, -$400. The next short ran 10.25 points to my target for +$1,025.

Friday my setup printed ahead of the New York bell. One ES long on my 25K eval, +12 points, +$600. On paper that same morning I practiced a 2 ES long for +23 points, +$2,300.

That's 9 trades kept in 3 logs: eval +$600, funded +$100, paper +$3,425. Paper is practice, so it never gets added to the real numbers. Everything here is before fees.

New York is still my main session. I don't stop looking for my setup outside it.

When you practice on paper, do you size it like real money or bigger?
